newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African truth body to ignore apology deadline.
newsitem.headline: S.African truth body to ignore apology deadline.

text.p: South Africa's truth commission said on Wednesday it would ignore a deadline later in the day set by the National Party (Nats) for an unconditional apology by commission chairman Archbishop Desmond Tutu.
The Nats, led by F.W. de Klerk, demanded on Monday that Tutu apologise by noon (1000 GMT) on Wednesday for having criticised the party's presentation on apartheid to the commission last month.
The party also demanded the resignation of deputy chairman Alex Boraine, who it said had made similar remarks violating the commission's charter to remain politically impartial.
Asked in a state radio interview on Monday if the commission would ignore the deadline, Boraine replied:

"Absolutely...We have 17 commissioners in every different part of the country and its simply impossible to bring them together at inconvenience and expense to discuss a matter really we are not persuaded needs that drastic attention."

The Nats objected to what they called aggressive grilling by the commission of de Klerk over the responsibility of cabinet ministers for apartheid-era atrocities. De Klerk said such atrocities as murder and torture were never official policy.

The party said Tutu and Boraine, in comments to a news conference after de Klerk's testimony, had effectively found the party guilty of abuses. It said the commission's handling of the African National Congress had by contrast been friendly and warm.
Boraine denied on Monday that he had over-stepped the commission mandate at any point.
"I was focusing on the need for political accountability," he said.

"We've had a number of senior policemen who have said they did what did on the clear understanding they were following the lead and the instructions of their political masters. What we're trying to ascertain is, where does the buck stop," Boraine said
A spokeswoman for the Nats, Sheila Camerer, said that if the commission ignorned the deadline the party would consult its lawyers on legal action.
"We believe it's very necessary to clear the matter up. We're saying we want to establish fair play," she said.
